text:
mira.dev: Heads-up — I'm seeing the provider upgrade in the release branch that touches aws provider -> 4.x. Can we hold the automated apply for the 02:00 change window until we validate the IAM plan?
jon.k: 02:00 window still good, but +1 on hold until we confirm no policy drift. which PR is this?
mira.dev: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/pulls/4321 — main change is provider version bump and a small route53 module attribute rename. Plan attached below.
deploy-bot: preflight check for branch infra/feature/provider-upgrade detected.
deploy-bot: terraform plan exit code 0. Summary: ~+3 -1 resources. Potential provider behavior: aws_route53_record attribute change (name -> fqdn).
samg: can you paste the plan lines for the IAM roles? want to ensure no role policy reattachments.
mira.dev: ```
# excerpt from plan
~ aws_iam_role.redwood-deploy
  assume_role_policy: "(sensitive)" => "(sensitive)"
~ aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.deploy-attach
  role: "old-name" => "old-name" # no replacement
```
lena.ops: If provider changes semantics we sometimes see diffy reorders; recommend pinning provider to 3.75.0 in the module and re-run plan. That avoids churn in the change window.
jon.k: Agree. Can we snap a provider pin in a hotfix branch and run a canary apply in staging? If staging plan is clean we proceed with 02:00.
mira.dev: I'll open quick revert/pin PR now. Pushing provider pin in module root:
```terraform
required_providers {
  aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 3.75.0" }
}
```
deploy-bot: note: apply queue currently shows 6 pending jobs. If we delay, we'll re-slot this change to next quiet window.
samg: Also let's split the apply: wave-1 = iam + secrets (low blast), wave-2 = network + route53. That way if route53 rename surprises us we can rollback only second wave.
lena.ops: +1 on split. Add a manual approval step in the deploybot workflow between waves.
jon.k: Who will approve wave-1? @samg?
samg: I can approve wave-1. After that I'll run a smoke script to confirm IAM permissions and lambda invocations.
mira.dev: staging plan after pin looks clean — no IAM replacements and route53 change is just attribute mapping. I'm scheduling the hotfix PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/pulls/4322
deploy-bot: scheduled apply for hotfix branch in staging at 23:30 UTC. Will wait for manual trigger to promote to prod change window.
jon.k: For prod, keep the 02:00 window but move network wave to +20 minutes after IAM apply to watch telemetry. Also annotate release notes: "Provider pin to avoid breaking route53 attribute rename; follow-up upgrade tracked in RFC-2026."
mira.dev: noted — adding release notes entry and RFC link.
samg: once wave-1 is applied I'll run `scripts/iam-smoke.sh` and post results here. If green, I'll approve wave-2. If route53 shows unexpected drift, we revert the module change and re-run plan.
lena.ops: reminder: ensure state lock health. If we need to cancel an apply, use deploy-bot abort and then run `terraform force-unlock` only with oncall signoff.
jon.k: OK — plan: pin provider (PR 4322), run staging canary, split prod apply into two waves with manual approval between them, keep +20 minute buffer, add release note and RFC link.
mira.dev: sounds good. I'll post status updates. Thanks all :thumbsup:
samg: posted smoke run: all checks green (invocations=ok, assume-role=ok). Approving wave-2 when ready.
deploy-bot: prod apply wave-1 started by mira.dev (apply id abcd-1234).
deploy-bot: prod apply wave-1 completed successfully.
samg: wave-1 smoke run passed in prod. Approving wave-2.
deploy-bot: prod apply wave-2 started by samg (apply id efgh-5678).
deploy-bot: prod apply wave-2 completed with 1 changed route53 record (attribute mapping only).
mira.dev: Verified traffic and DNS checks, all green. Closing thread and will file follow-up RFC for major aws provider upgrade testing.
jon.k: great work, team. Documenting postmortem notes in release board.
